parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of same-sex activity or gender expression, no sodomy statute, no documented border or facility restriction, and an official posture that is at least nominally welcoming (tourism-ministry endorsement of an LGBT-welcome campaign, ministry pressure on media mockery, UPR acceptances, long-running Pride, visible scene in two cities). But the UPR acceptances are paper only: no anti-discrimination or hate-crime statute, no complaint mechanism, no documented remedy of any kind. Against that, the record documents police targeting of trans women in one city (forced naked bathing in stagnant water, displacement, extortion) and a survey finding 38% of trans women arrested, over 90% for being trans — state-tolerated targeting with zero recourse. That is largely local-sphere (street sex work), which limits its traveller weight, but a visibly trans visitor stopped by police has no protection. Custody placement for non-surgical trans detainees is unresolved (surgery-gated transfer remark only) — an open question, weighted lightly. Elevated Risk: worse than the 0.55 tier where remedies actually operate, better than 0.35 where police sweeps routinely reach foreign travellers.
